articleTitle: Sub-Synchronous Control Interaction in Grid-Forming VSCs with Droop Control
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper analyzes the sub-synchronous control interaction of droop-controlled grid-forming voltage-source converters (VSCs). The complex-valued impedance model of the droop-controlled VSC in the stationary frame is proposed first, based on which the grid-VSC interaction is characterized. It is revealed that the sub-synchronous resonances can be induced in stiff grids, owing to the interactions of inner voltage control loop and the outer power control loop. Experimental tests corroborate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: The control strategy of Harmonic suppression of Photovoltaic grid-connected inverter based on PI+MPR
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In the field of grid-connected photovoltaic power generation, because the output PWM carrier of the inverter circuit is relatively low and the inverter circuit contains a large number of non-linear switching semiconductor devices, the three-phase grid-connected current is prone to distortion, which seriously affects the safe and reliable operation of the power system. The traditional PI current loop control is mostly used in the control system of the photovoltaic inverter circuit, although the control strategy can track quickly. Instruction current, but the ability to suppress harmonics is weak. Based on this, in order to suppress harmonic current and ensure good dynamic response, this paper proposes a harmonic suppression scheme of photovoltaic grid-connected inverters based on PI + proportional resonance control (MPR). By means of MATLAB/Simulink and experiments, it is proved that the scheme can not only improve the dynamic response performance of the system, but also reduce the specific sub-harmonics in the grid-connected current.

articleTitle: Comparison Analysis on EMI Sources of MMC Under NLM and CPS-PWM Strategies
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) is a serious problem for Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC). The large quantity of switching devices in MMC bring in lots of EMI sources which are associated with modulation strategies. Two most commonly used modulation strategies for MMC are Nearest Level Modulation (NLM) and Carrier Phase-Shift Pulse Width Modulation (CPS-PWM). A comparison analysis on EMI sources' performance under NLM and CPS-PWM strategies are conducted by geometric deduction. Analysis and simulation results reveal that NLM has a better EMI performance in PWM frequency range than CPS-PWM.

articleTitle: A Variable Switching Frequency PWM Control Method for Single-Phase MMC
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Traditional constant switching frequency pulse-width-modulation (CSFPWM) would cause high electromagnetic interference (EMI) peak ratio and high switching loss. This letter introduces a method to make the carrier frequency of the single-phase modular multilevel inverter (MMC) change with the output current by using variable switching frequency PWM (VSFPWM). By adjusting the carrier frequency of single-phase MMC, the switching period of PWM pulse based on carrier signal comparison is adjusted to control the switching frequency of single-phase MMC driven by PWM pulse. When the load current is zero, the switching frequency is maximum, and when the load current is maximum, the switching frequency is minimum. In addition, the average switching frequency is equal to the fixed switching frequency in the control cycle. This method aiming at switching loss optimization in high power application also has benefit in reducing system conduction EMI because of the wider current harmonic spectrum distribution.

articleTitle: A rotation-based capacitor-voltage-balancing method for modular multilevel converters
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Modular multilevel converters (MMC) are widely applied in HVDC projects. To ensure that MMC works properly, sub-module (SM) capacitor voltages must be balanced. This paper proposes a voltage balancing method, which alternates the driving signals on the IGBTs of SMs in fundamental period or carrier period, to balance the capacitor voltages. Under normal operating conditions, this proposed method doesn't need the capacitor voltages of SMs and arm currents information, therefore it effectively decreases the hardware cost and software complexity of MMC system, and also improves the system reliability. The proposed method is validated by constructing a 5-level 1kW single-phase experimental platform in the laboratory. The experimental results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of proposed voltage balancing method.

articleTitle: Enhanced Diode-rectifier HVDC for Offshore Wind Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: As a promising scheme for offshore wind power transmission, diode rectifier based high voltage dc has raised wide attention recently. But the design of DR-HVDC is mainly based on the traditional line commutated converter HVDC, which required large amount of reactive power and generated high harmonics. In this paper, an enhanced DR-HVDC is proposed to reduce the harmonic and reactive power consumption by utilizing 24 pulses bridge and transformer with decreased leakage reactance. Meanwhile, the filter designed for enhanced DR-HVDC is also introduced, which can save the space required for reactive power compensation. Finally, the enhanced DR-HVDC with Type IV wind farm controlled by distributed phase lock loop scheme is built in PSCAD/EMTDC, which proved the effectiveness and superiority of proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A Sequence Impedance Modeling of VSG With Consideration of Inner Loops Control
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Virtual synchronous generators (VSG), as one of the most widely used inverter control schemes, has been studied in the perspective of impedance modeling in recent years. In this paper, the sequence impedance model of VSG is built, taking the inner loops control into account, to make it more accurate than previous researches. Based on the model built in this paper, this paper points out that the inner loops should not be ignored since it has a relatively enormous influence on characteristics of the output impedance of VSGs. Finally, simulation results validate the accuracy of this model and prepare for further study of stability issues of VSGs.

articleTitle: Near-Synchornous Resonance Interaction of Paralleled Grid-forming Converters in Islanded Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The natural synchronous resonance issue is one of the key features of grid-forming converters. It is caused by the frequency-shifting nature of power calculation when adopting power based synchronization mechanism. This paper is a report of a 33kW power-hardware-in-the-loop test, whose results show that not only synchronous resonance but also near-synchronous resonance phenomenon can occur due to interaction between the active power control loops of grid-forming converters when operating in islanded mode. In addition to that, the test results also show that the different resonance modes are highly related to the cutting frequency design of the low-pass filter used in the power calculation process. In this paper, analytical model is established to figure out the root cause of such interaction. A preliminary design guideline for the filter design is also proposed to avoid such unstable interaction.

articleTitle: Deviation-Free Frequency Control of MMC-MTDC Converter Based on Improved VSG
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: As an important issue of the future AC-DC hybrid power system, the research of coordinated control between MMC-MTDC transmission system and AC network is attracting more and more attention. Based on the conventional virtual synchronous generator (CVSG) control method, the converter connected with AC network can simulate the traditional synchronous generator participating in primary frequency regulation of AC system, but its frequency control accuracy needs to be improved. To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved frequency regulation control strategy for the virtual synchronous generator (IVSG) converter. This strategy introduces the frequency deviation based on the inertial parameters and damping parameters in the CVSG control, which enables the grid-connected converter to cooperate with the thermal power unit to participate in the AC system's error-free frequency regulation in real time, and then realize the high-precision frequency support of the converter to the AC system frequency. Based on the Opal-RT simulation platform, a five-terminal 31-level MMC-MTDC transmission system model including the cluster wind field is built. The proposed control strategy is verified by real-time simulation under two operating conditions: DC power change and AC load fluctuation. The simulation results show that the proposed control strategy can effectively improve the frequency regulation accuracy of AC system.

articleTitle: A Transformerless Hybrid Modular Step-up DC/DC Converter for Bipolar and Symmetrical Monopolar HVDC Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Serving as DC transformer in HVDC grid, high-voltage and high-power DC/DC converter is one of the most important HVDC devices. This paper proposes a novel hybrid modular transformerless step-up DC/DC converter for symmetrical monopolar and bipolar HVDC grids interconnection, which can still operate even though a DC pole-to-ground short-circuit fault takes place. This DC/DC converter features high efficiency, low capital costs and small footprint. Operation principle is introduced and simulation results from MATLAB/Simulink verify the feasibility of the proposed DC/DC topology.

articleTitle: Open-Circuit Fault Diagnosis and Fault-Tolerant Control with Sequential Indirect Model Predictive Control for Modular Multilevel Converters
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant control are significant for the reliability of an MMC system, which usually has a large number of switching devices and high potential of operation failure. This paper proposes a simple fault diagnosis method for sub-module open-circuit faults and a new fault-tolerant control method. The proposed methods combine a novel sequential indirect MPC structure with sorting algorithm. Different from the well-known solutions, we detect and locate open-circuit faults in any sub-module efficiently with the maximum voltage output of the capacitor voltage sorting result, which is based on the physical characteristics of circuits when capacitor voltage rises. Thereafter, a new fault-tolerant control solution based on MPC is implemented through modifying circuit structure and control algorithm. The proposed methods are easy to implement and add little computational complexity to the control algorithm. Finally, the MATLAB/Simulink verification results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed solutions.

articleTitle: A Study on VSC- HVDC Based Black Start Method
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In this paper, a detailed study on the VSC-HVDC based black start method is carried out with three main aspects: (1) design the black start strategy of the VSCs at each terminal based on analysis of the demands for black start capability; (2) give an overview of the process to restore the operation of the VSC-HVDC system; (3) Verify the expected performance of VSC-HVDC with active charging strategy by simulating the entire black start process on a two-terminal VSC-HVDC system using PSCAD/EMTDC, which includes “soft start-up” the transformer with gradually increased AC voltage. The simulation results demonstrate that the VSC-HVDC is an ideal black start power source with the advantages of reduced restoration time, safe and smooth restoration etc.

articleTitle: Analysis and Control of Improved MMC With Symmetrical Super Capacitor Energy Storage System in EER Application
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Energy storage system becomes one of key components in the medium voltage grid with the ever-increasing development of renewable energy resources. This paper proposes an improved modular multilevel converter (IMMC) where symmetrical super capacitor energy storage banks are interfaced to the three-terminal power unit through a Buck/Boost converter. Six typical operation modes are taken into account and the control algorithms such as state of charge (SOC) equalization and sub-module capacitor balance based on carrier phase shift sine pulse width modulation (CPS-SPWM) are developed. Finally., the analysis and control strategies are verified through the MATLAB/Simulink simulation results and down-scaled prototype experimental results.

articleTitle: Online Monitoring and Balancing for MMC Capacitor Aging
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Metallized film capacitor (MFC) is widely used to maintain the stability of sub-module voltage in modular multilevel converter (MMC). Capacitor aging is likely to lead to a decrease in the capacitance value and an increase in equivalent series resistance (ESR). And it will increase the voltage fluctuation and rise the temperature, which may accelerate the aging of capacitors and cause the open-circuit of power electronic devices in serious circumstances. However, the traditional on-line monitoring methods for capacitor aging are not suitable for MMC because of the higher occupation for computing resources and hardware resources. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an on-line monitoring method for capacitor aging degree without installing any additional device. Then a balancing strategy is designed to balance the relative aging degree of capacitors, which can reduce the switching frequency of sub-module with sever aging state and extending the lives of capacitors. The simulation results confirm the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Modelling of Output Admittance Coupling Between Shunt Active Power Filters and Non-linear Loads
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Nowadays Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) system still suffers from stability issue which heavily detect its performance. In this paper, an improved system level model is proposed to investigate the coupling effect that will cause the system level instability. This model describes the coupling effect with an additional output admittance and shows system stability more directly. In order to investigate the correctness of the proposed method, a grid including the SAPF and a non-linear load is modelled with both conventional approach and proposed modeling method. Simulations are carried out with the same parameters. Results show that the instability of the grid current observed in the simulation results is not reflected in the stability analysis based on the conventional model. On the other hand, the stability analysis with the new model matches the simulation results very well. Also, further verification is made by a frequency-sweep result, which proves the accuracy of proposed model.

articleTitle: A Novel Soft-Switching Bidirectional DC-DC Converter With High Voltage-Gain for Grid-Connected Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: A novel soft-switching bidirectional DC-DC converter with high voltage-gain using dual equal PWM plus phase-shifted control is proposed for grid-connected energy storage system in this paper. The high voltage-gain can be achieved without high turns ratio of the transformer due to the employment of a current doubler and a voltage doubler. Two interleaved buck-boost bidirectional dc-dc converters (BDCs) are adopted to reduce the current ripple in the energy storage side. The inherent zero voltage switching (ZVS) is achieved by proper design of the magnetizing inductance. The associated control is adopted to achieve the decoupling of voltage-matching and power flow control. A 40-60 V/280 V 700-W prototype is constructed with 50-kHz switching frequency to verify the effectiveness of the proposed converter. The consistency between the analysis results and experimental results further proves its merits.

articleTitle: Analysis of Inertia Mechanism of Grid-tied Photovoltaic Power Generation System With Virtual Inertia Control
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In the absence of energy storage, photovoltaics (PV) also need to provide inertia support to the power electronic power system. Based on the DC bus voltage droop control to provide the inertia of the converter, two improved virtual inertia control strategies are proposed. From the perspective of DC bus voltage U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</sub> and system virtual inertia coefficient H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</sub> under load disturbance, the advantages and disadvantages of three virtual inertia control strategies and the influence of control parameters on system inertia are analyzed. The conventional droop control is a full-band response load disturbance, and the inertia coefficient H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dp</sub>increases with the droop coefficient K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dp</sub> increases, but the DC bus voltage cannot be restored to the initial set value. The improved low-pass filter control (ILPFC) only responds to the load disturbance in the low frequency band. In fact, a delay link is introduced on the basis of the conventional droop control to slow down the frequency response speed, and increasing the K1 or ω1 can also increase the system inertia effect. The improved high-pass filter control (IHPFC) only responds to load disturbances in the high frequency band, overcomes the problem that the conventional droop control cannot restore the DC bus voltage to the initial set value. Meanwhile, increasing Kh or decreasing ω h can also improve the system inertia support. Finally, the effectiveness of the control strategy and the correctness of the analysis conclusion are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Cost-Reducing Optimization Strategies of Electrical Trains
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The development of Railway Smart Grids (RSGs) has multi-fold benefits [1]. Trains are flexible demands and thus it is possible to have a multitude of velocity profiles satisfying the same end-to-end time constraints. This opens up the opportunities of cost of energy optimization in RSGs in addition to energy optimization in electric railways. In this paper, we have proposed the idea of transaction of energy between the trains and external loads when there is a difference between the day-ahead and real-time electricity price. This is made possible by the flexibility of the power demand of the trains. This case has been analyzed on Acela express running on Northeast Corridor for different trips. The results show promise in that the participating entities can make profit on successful price negotiation.

articleTitle: Accurate Measurement of Converter Sequence Impedance by Active Cancellation of Coupling over Frequency
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Impedance-based analysis plays important role in assessing the stability and dynamics of grid-connected inverters and related systems. Measuring the inverter impedance is, however, not straightforward due to the load effect caused by the power grid. The power grid interacts with the inverter and produces additional (mirrored) frequency harmonics thus distorting the impedance measurements when applying conventional measurement techniques. This paper proposes an active-power filtering method to minimize the undesired load effect caused by the power grid in the measured impedance. Applying the method, the inverter output impedance can be reliably measured under non-ideal grid conditions.

articleTitle: A parameter coordination method for fault current limiting impedance of flexible DC converter station based on Voltage stress analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: DC circuit breakers (DCCB) need high operate speed and current break ability because fault current of flexible dc grid rising fast and conventional half-bridge Modular Multilevel Converters (MMC) are short of over current tolerance ability. Fault current limiter (FCL) can retrain fault current when short-circuit fault is identified, and reduce the requirement of DCCB. The equivalent circuit of MMC with FCL is proposed in this paper, and then the fault current and voltage stress of FCL with different types of fault limiting impedance are calculated; voltage stress characteristics of FCL with the change of parameters are analyzed; a parameter coordination method for different types of fault limiting impedance is proposed. The method proposed in this paper can improve fault current limiting ability of FCL without change topological structure. Works in this paper are verified through PSCAD/EMTDC simulation.

articleTitle: Influence of Stray Capacitance on Dynamic Test Results of Power Semiconductor devices
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Stray capacitance in semiconductor device dynamic test platform affects the switching waveform, especially in the testing of SiC semiconductor devices, which has a faster switching than silicon semiconductor devices. During turn-on and turn-off process, the collector-emitter voltage changes rapidly, and stray capacitance shunts a portion of the total current, which causes the measurement of a distorted result. In order to investigate the effect of stray capacitance and voltage change on current measurement results, an equivalent circuit model considering parasitic capacitance is built. Theoretical analysis shows that stray capacitance causes undesirable current distortion during switching transient. Experimental results verified the correctness of theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Hybrid Series-connected HVDC System Faults Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Multi-infeed cascaded hybrid series-connected DC transmission technology combines the advantages of line commutated converters and voltage sourced converters. Hybrid DC transmission is expected to play an important role in future power transmission systems. It is of great importance to understand the system's behavior under steady and transient states. This paper thoroughly examines the system's responses under different types of faults. The benefits of having such a hybrid system are also highlighted through the fault analysis. In order to cope with the AC system three-phase fault, based on the comparison, a new thyristor based DC energy dissipation device has been proposed. Simulation results show that this device could protect the VSCs from severe faults.

articleTitle: A Novel Interface Modeling Method of Power Hardware-in-the-loop Simulation for MMC-HVDC System Based on ITM and DIM Switching
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In this paper, based on the comparative analysis of the interface characteristics between ideal transformer model (ITM) method and damping impedance method (DIM), a novel interface modeling method based on ITM and DIM switching is proposed to improve the stability and simulation accuracy of power hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) simulation for MMC-HVDC system. According to the structure principle of two interface algorithms, the ITM and DIM switching method is proposed to realize the effective switching of interface characteristics, which can be achieved by changing additional impedance parameters of DIM. The calculation process of equivalent impedance for the MMC AC side is simplified to realize the real-time impedance matching of DIM, and the switching criterion and solution of maloperation are designed based on the interface stability of ITM. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control methods are verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Junction Temperature Analysis of Press-Pack IG-BTs of Modular Multilevel Converter Based on Electro-Thermal Coupling Model
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Press- pack insulated gate bipolar transistor (PP-IGBT) has been being widely used in modular multilevel converter based high voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) systems. However, after a long-term cyclic thermal stress, the material of the PP-IGBT will gradually encounter fatigue failure, which will affect the reliability of the device. Therefore, information of junction temperature fluctuation is vital for lifetime evaluation of PP-IGBT and stable operation of MMC. In this paper, the power loss of IGBT in the sub-module (SM) of MMC is analyzed firstly, then the thermal network model of PP-IGBT is proposed and established in Simulink. Based on the model, junction temperature characteristics of PP-IGBT are simulated in combination with specific MMC system. Finally, the finite element method (FEM) model is built in COM-SOL to verify the results. The simulation results show that the non-continuous sinusoidal current flowing through IGBT leads to the fluctuation of the junction temperature. The rise rate, transient time, steady-state value and fluctuation range of junction temperature in IGBT are positively correlated with the current flowing through the IGBT. The temperature fluctuation characteristics of the FEM model verify the correctness and effectiveness of thermal network model established in this paper.

articleTitle: An Improved Droop Control Method for Distributed Diesel Generators without Intercommunication under the Disaster Condition
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Under disaster condition, emergency diesel generators play an important role in ensuring power supply and disaster relief. The state of the AC bus under the island is determined by the output characteristics of the distributed diesel generators (DGs). The improved drooping method proposed in the paper introduces PI-based non-communication secondary control based on the traditional droop control to achieve the stability of the frequency and voltage of the AC bus under the disaster condition. On the basis of coordinating diesel DGs equal-distribution of active power, it is also possible to maintain the AC bus in the rated state well in the system state transition, and avoid the fluctuation of the bus voltage frequency.

articleTitle: Capacitance Calculation of Overhead Transmission Line Based on Moment Method
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In this paper, the capacitance parameter of the overhead transmission lines is calculated by the moment method (MoM), which is based on the image method of electromagnetic theory. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by an overhead transmission line model, which has analytical solution. The comparison results show that the relative error between the MoM and analytical solution is small, which shows the accuracy of the program based on the MoM. Then the proposed MoM is applied to calculate the distributed capacitance parameters of three typical overhead transmission lines.

articleTitle: A Staged Current Limiting Scheme of Hybrid DC Circuit Breaker for HVDC Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Several half-bridge modular multilevel converter (HB-MMC) HVDC projects have been put into operation in recent years. When the DC side faults, the sharp rise current will easily cause the damage of the converters. This paper proposes a new staged current-limiting HVDC circuit breaker (DCCB) scheme, which is based on the existing hybrid DCCB. The new scheme can not only put into current-limiting quickly after the fault but also maintain current-limiting for a period, which reserves enough time for DC protection judgment. Meanwhile, it can reduce the difficulty of DCCB to cut off the fault line through self-bypass design. The feasibility and validity of the proposed scheme are verified to be applicable for HVDC fault isolation requirements by PSCAD/EMTDC simulation results.

articleTitle: Reliability calculation model of converter station for MMC-HVDC Power Transmission system and its application
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Modular multilevel converter based high voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) technology as the new generation of DC transmission technology, has been developed and applied globally. With the development of the technology, the reliability evaluation of MMC-HVDC transmission system has become increasingly important. The reliability modeling and analysis of converter station are mainly concerned. The fault tree analysis (FTA) method is adopted. Firstly, the reliability index and calculation method are presented. Then, the fault tree model of converter station is established in isograph software based on equipment list and the basic reliability data of each component. Furthermore, the reliability level of the converter station is calculated, and the components that most affect the reliability level are obtained by sensitivity analysis.

articleTitle: Fast Detection Method of DC Short Circuit Fault of MMC-HVDC Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper presents a fast detection method of DC short-circuit faults of high voltage direct current based on modular multilevel converter (MMC-HVDC) grid, which is characterized by fault identification according to the voltage change rate of the arm inductance of MMC converter station. When the internal fault occurs, the voltage change rate of the arm inductance is positive and not less than the set value; when the external fault occurs, the voltage change rate of the arm inductance is positive and not more than the set value. Then according to the change of transient current at the outlet of each DC line in MMC converter station, the DC line with faults in the area can be judged. Taking the outlet of any DC line in the converter station as the detection point, if the change of transient current at the detection point is positive, the fault occurs on the positive direction of the original current; if the change of transient current at the detection point is negative, the fault occurs on the reverse direction of the original current. The invention can detect the fault within 1ms or even shorter time after the fault occurs, and determine the location of the fault line.

articleTitle: Analysis of Transfer Operation between Metallic and Ground Return Configurations for Multi-terminal HVDC Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper mainly focuses on the transfer operation between monopolar ground and metallic return configurations for multi-terminal high voltage direct current (HVDC) systems. For an HVDC system with more than two converters, there are several transfer sequences. How to choose a proper sequence seems to be a difficulty. To solve this problem, this paper takes an three-terminal HVDC system as an example. Different transfer sequences are discussed in details. The control method of transfer operation is also proposed to ensure the safe operation of the exemplified HVDC system. Numerical simulation studies with PSCAD/EMTDC are carried out to verify the theoretical results drawn by this paper.

articleTitle: Multiple mode operation and control for VSG interfacing DC distribution system
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: DC distribution system at low and medium voltage level is undergoing rapid development, driven by the growth of power electronic technology and integration of distributed generation. Virtual synchronous generator (VSG), which can operate in grid-connected mode and islanded mode, provides a convenient interconnecting interface between DC distribution system and AC grid. However, the multiple mode operation and transition of VSG in grid-connected and islanded process is not thoroughly studied, including start-up and reconnection. On the other hand, most research into oscillation mechanism in the past does not consider the outer frequency droop loop. To address these issues, this paper proposed to use VSG in DC distribution system. A phase and frequency regulator is designed to achieve smooth start-up and a method is proposed to realize reconnection of VSG with AC grid in the current research. Stability analysis considering the frequency droop loop is also conducted, based on which proper damping is selected to mitigate the oscillation in transition and grid-connected mode. The proposed strategy is verified by electro-magnetic type simulation on PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Current Ripple Estimation for 3-Level ILCL Filtered Grid-Connected Inverters with the SVPWM or the DPWM Method
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The improved LCL filter (ILCL) is widely applied on transformer-less 3-level grid-connected PV inverters to suppress the common current flowing into the grid. Since the neutral point of the DC bus is directly connected to the common point of the filter capacitor, the current ripple distribution with ILCL filter is different from that with the LCL filter. In this paper, we analysis the current ripple firstly for the 3-level ILCL- filtered inverter with the space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) or the discontinuous pulse width modulation (DPWM) in consideration of the filter inductance variation. Finally, the analysis result is verified by the experiment.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Pattern of Transient Energy Flow under DC Fault of MMC-HVDC Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis method of electromagnetic transient energy flow for modular multilevel converter based high voltage direct current grid. This method can extract the features of transient energy flow of the key components such as AC side, DC side, three-phase upper and lower bridge arm inductors, energy storage elements and DC side inductor under the condition of DC side faults. The characteristics of each part of electromagnetic transient energy are analyzed, along with the key factors affecting the evolution of them, in order to provide a basis for the optimal design of DC short-circuit fault detection and protection strategy. The four-terminal MMC-HVDC grid simulation model is built in PSCAD. The transient energy flow of the system under different scenarios for DC side fault is analyzed in details. The simulation results show that the transient energy flow and its evolution characteristics can provide a new way for the fast location of DC short-circuit fault and the optimization of protection strategy.

articleTitle: Analysis on key technical characteristics of chongqing-hubei back-to-back grid-connected project
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper introduced the general construction situation of VSC-HVDC projects in China and summarized the technical features of these projects. Taking the Chongqing-Hubei back-to-back grid-connected project as an example, the key technical characteristics in its engineering design and control and protection function are explained. The functions and principles of these key technical features are analyzed, as well as the differences with other projects. The purpose of this paper is to take the chongqing-hubei project as an example to analyze the key technologies of the VSC-HVDC system, so as to provide some references for understanding the VSC-HVDC project.

articleTitle: NSGA-III Based Controller Parameter Design for Optimizing Impedance of VF Controller MMC
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The positive damping characteristic of a modular multilevel converter (MMC) is important for improving the stability of an MMC based system. However, it is difficult to optimize the impedance characteristics of the MMC by adjusting the controller parameters, due to the complexity of the existing impedance model. This paper investigates the influence of the voltage-frequency(VF) controller on the impedance of an MMC, in which the relationship between open loop controlled impedance and VF controlled impedance is established. Based on the proposed impedance model, Non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm III (NSGA-III) is used to optimize the parameters of the VF controller, which makes the MMC positive damping in chosen frequencies. The time domain simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC verify the proposed impedance model and the optimized results.

articleTitle: An Improved Droop Control Method for VSC- MTDC Considering Power Mismatch Allocation
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Converter control of voltage-source-converter multi-terminal DC (VSC-MTDC) grids interconnecting offshore wind farms over long distance is an important research area grabbing much attention in academia and industry. When a converter outage happens in VSC-MTDC grids or the active power injected into DC grids varies, how to determine the power mismatch allocation is a critical issue. To overcome the problem of inaccurate estimation of power mismatch distribution based on local voltage measurements, this paper proposes an improved droop control method that can establishes a common DC voltage signal across the VSC-MTDC grids. Further, a method to determine the droop constants is also developed. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy on power sharing of is verified by time-domain simulation studies of a four-terminal VSC-MTDC system in PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Impedance-based Stability Analysis of Two- Terminal Cascaded Voltage Source Converter System
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The voltage source converters (VSC) have been widely applied in power systems and the stability issue has become a hot topic in recent years. This paper focuses on the stability analysis of dc bus of the systems based on grid connected voltage source converters, which contain single VSC stations and two-terminal cascaded system. The DC side impedance model of each VSC has been established. The stability of single VSC system has been analyzed by determining whether the closed loop impedance has right-half-plane (RHP) pole or not. And, the stability of two-terminal cascaded system is determined by Nyquist Criterion. How the parameters influence the stability of the systems has been analyzed in detail. Finally, the impedance models and stability analysis have been verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Reactive Power and Voltage Support Capability of Distribution PV power station
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: At present, the reactive power supporting ability of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power stations wins much attentions, and its corresponding evaluation has important theoretical and practical significance. However, there are many factors, including the access modes, the number of access points, the access voltage level and the power factor, can affect the reactive power supporting ability, which makes it difficult to comprehensive evaluate the reactive power supporting ability of distributed PV power station. In view of this, a comprehensive evaluation method is proposed in this study, it builds a comprehensive evaluation index system fully considering variety of influencing factor. By using the data collected from the typical PV power station verifies the proposed comprehensive evaluation index system and reactive power supporting ability evaluation method.

articleTitle: RL model algorithm-based fault location for DC distribution networks
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: A fault location algorithm is proposed to guarantee the reliable operation of DC distribution based on voltage source converter (VSC). The overviews of DC distribution topology and its fault characteristics are presented. The feasibility of R-L model algorithm for DC distribution networks is analyzed. A double-terminal fault location algorithm is proposed to deal with the fault resistance. The results of simulation verify the feasibility of proposed method. With the 15 ms of fault records, the proposed method can accurately locate the fault point and the relative error is within 0.05%. The proposed method is immune from the fault resistance.

articleTitle: New Cross-Switch Multilevel Inverter with Self-Voltage Balance and Boost Ability for Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The new cross-switch multilevel inverter (CSMLI) consisting of n cross-switch cells (CSCs) and a three-level T-type converter is proposed in this paper. The capacitors in CSCs can get self-voltage balance without auxiliary methods. Moreover, the output level and boost factor of the proposed topology can be increased with additional CSCs, and the highest voltage stress among switches maintains at a low degree meanwhile. The operation principles and self-voltage balance are illustrated in detail. The comparative study among different multilevel inverters is also conducted in this paper, demonstrating its certain merits on reduced components and voltage stress and the suitability for microgrid. Finally, the nine-level prototype of the proposed topology with 1kVA rated output are implemented to verify the feasibility and performance.

articleTitle: A Soft Open Points with Direct AC-AC Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Soft open points (SOP) is a new flexible interconnection equipment which can replace the conventional tie switches installed in the distribution network. SOP can continuously and precisely regulate power flow and optimize the voltage profile of feeders to enhance the controllability and flexibility of the distribution network. This paper proposes an SOP based on a compact direct AC-AC modular multilevel converter (direct MMC-SOP). Compared with the SOP based on back-to-back connected MMC (MMC-SOP), the direct MMC-SOP can save 25% submodules and 50% arm inductors. Therefore, the investment cost and volume of the whole SOP system can be dramatically reduced which is more suitable for distribution networks being close to the city center. The topology structure and operating principle of direct MMC-SOP are firstly presented in this paper. Next, the control scheme including capacitor voltage balancing control and circulating current suppression control is elaborately described. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the characteristics of direct MMC-SOP and corresponding control strategy.

articleTitle: Calculation Method of Harmonic Grid-connected MMC-HVDC and Large AC system
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper proposes a harmonic calculation method, describes the methodologies to carry out steady-state harmonic performance studies at PCC point. Based on a small signal harmonic current and voltage sources injected to a large-scale AC system and MMC converters, the method can be used for harmonic characteristic calculation of the grid-connected MMC-HVDC and large AC system at Point of Common Coupling (PCC). To verify the proposed method, a typical offshore wind farm integrated into the AC system using a MMC-HVDC link model is built in the electromagnetic transient simulation software PSCAD/EMTDC. Simulation results of individual harmonic distortion (Dn) and Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) are calculated and compared with the analytical calculation values. The comparison results show correction and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Application of Solid-State Circuit Breaker in Selective Relay Protection of Marine DC Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: DC distribution electric propulsion is the trend of ship power development in the future. The problem of selective relay protection for bus-connected equipment has not been properly solved, which directly threatens the safety of navigation. Therefore, on the basis of analyzing the short-circuit fault principle of marine DC distribution system and the simulation and experimental verification, a relay protection scheme using solid-state circuit breaker instead of the bus-tie fast fuse is proposed. The scheme uses high-speed interruption to isolate the impact of fault on bus voltage on the normal side to ensure the continuity of power supply and navigation safety. Finally, the realization method of selective relay protection for DC distribution system and the strategy of power supply recovery after fault are put forward, which meet the requirements of marine power engineering application.

articleTitle: Economic benefit evaluation and incentive strategy research on Wind energy and BESS jointly participating in peak shaving auxiliary service market
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The battery energy storage station (BESS) is developing from the demonstration project to the stage of business promotion. Due to the unsound Economic benefit evaluation, which restricts the large-scale promotion and construction of BESS. This paper establishes the life cycle cost and income model of BESS and uses the dynamic investment payback period, net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR) and other economic indicators to analyze the economy of offshore wind power with BESS in peak shaving auxiliary service market. At the same time, aiming at stimulating the enthusiasm of the wind farm to allocate energy storage, we studied the improvement of the market regulation rules and government subsidies. The research results can provide an engineering economic reference for the investment decision of BESS and the government to guide the development of energy storage.

articleTitle: Research on Restart Strategy and Scheme of Flexible Medium Voltage DC Distribution Network without DC Circuit Breaker after Faults
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In the system without DC circuit breaker, the equivalent capacitor voltage and the fault current of hybrid converter before and after blocking based on full bridge sub-module and double active bridge under the bipolar short circuit fault are deduced, and the analytical formulas are obtained. The transient characteristics of the system before and after locking are analyzed, and the system restart process after fault clearance is analyzed. In order to accelerate the restart process after fault clearing, a fast restart strategy for hybrid converter is proposed. The strategy points out that during the blocking period of the hybrid converter, while energy storage provides power support for essential loads such as data center, the capacitor voltages of sub-modules during the blocking period are adjusted to shorten the restart time and ensure that the system can restart safely and reliably. A simulation model is built on the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation platform to verify the correctness of the strategy.

articleTitle: Broadband Sub-synchronous Signal Extraction and Analysis of the Key Parameters
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Recently, with the development of new energy power generation and power electronic technology, wind power are applied more and more widely, which has improved energy efficiency while bringing some influence on stability of the power grid. A large collection of Doubly-fed wind farms, together with series compensation on the line, will lead to resonance and produce sub-synchronous oscillation, which will harm the grid. Since the network structure of the actual wind power transmission system is complex, such sub-synchronous signal is broadband and time-varying, and its amplitude is small, leading to difficulties to be extracted. To address this issue, an effective sub-synchronous signal extraction method is proposed here, to apply to a parallel sub-synchronous resonance suppression device and its control strategy. Then the extraction method is compared with other methods to prove its superiority and implemented on hardware. The effectiveness of the sub-synchronous signal extraction method is also verified through a digital-hardware in-loop test. Moreover, the regulation of its valid key parameters is summarized through simulations on different working conditions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Valve Structure on Current Evolution of MMC-HVDC Bipolar Short Circuit Fault
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In recent years, flexible direct current transmission technology has shown broad application prospects in important fields such as renewable energy generation, multiterminal direct current transmission, and island power supply. Modular multilevel converter (MMC) has become the preferred topology for flexible DC transmission. However, a major challenge for the development of flexible DC grids is DC side fault analysis and protection. This paper considers the MMC-based high-voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) system as the research object. Firstly, the DC-side fault isolation principle of MMC system with different valve structures is expounded. And the valve structure classification is obtained through the RLC equivalent circuit model. Secondly, in order to more comprehensively evaluate DC-side fault blocking capacity of different valve structures, the transient energy analysis method is proposed to study the energy transfer characteristics of different regions (AC side, MMC station and DC side). Finally, a two-terminal MMC-HVDC model is established on PSCAD/EMTDC and the system transient energy transfer characteristics is analyzed in stages. The simulation results can provide practical guidance for fault protection and sub-module topology selection.

articleTitle: Study on Hardware-in-the-loop Model and Low Voltage Ride-through Characteristics of Photovoltaic Power Station
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In order to prevent large-scale disconnection accidents of photovoltaic power stations caused by voltage fluctuations and faults in power grids, low voltage ride-through characteristics and other detection tests are needed when photovoltaic power stations are connected to power grids. At present, field test and type test are the main methods of detection, but due to the limitation of detection devices and test conditions, the evaluation of low voltage ride-through characteristics of photovoltaic power stations still remains in the single-machine detection mode, which ignores the interaction between photovoltaic inverters and inverters, inverters and static var generator(SVG) devices. The test results cannot truly reflect the low voltage traversing characteristics of the photovoltaic power stations. Using RT-LAB hardware-in-the-loop simulation platform, real photovoltaic inverters and SVG controllers are introduced to build simulation models of photovoltaic power stations. The differences between single-machine detection of photovoltaic inverters and reactive power compensation devices and low-voltage ride-through characteristics detection of the whole station are compared and studied. The simulation results show that, compared with the stand-alone test, the whole station simulation modeling test method can reflect the voltage rise caused by the reactive power characteristics of photovoltaic inverters and SVG devices after the drop, and more truly reflect the low voltage traversing characteristics of photovoltaic power stations.

articleTitle: A Short-Circuit Current Calculation Method Based on Discrete Model for VSC-HVDC Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: A numerical calculation method for short-circuit current of voltage source converter based high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) grid based on discrete model is proposed in this paper. For VSC-HVDC grid based on modular multilevel converter (MMC), the equivalent circuit after DC short-circuit fault is analyzed. Based on the Backward Euler Method, the discrete models of inductance and capacitor in converter and lines is established. Besides, discrete model of converter stations under different fault types is formed. On this basis, the numerical solution algorithm for different types of fault currents in DC grids is designed. Based on the RT-lab platform, a four-terminal VSC-HVDC grid simulation model is built. The numerical solution calculation and electromagnetic model simulation results are compared and analyzed. It is verified that the fault current value can be accurately obtained based on the proposed model and fault current numerical solution algorithm. The calculation error is less than 5.5% compared to the simulation results.

articleTitle: Economic benefit evaluation and incentive strategy research on Wind energy and BESS jointly participating in reducing the forecast deviation penalty
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The battery energy storage system (BESS) is developing from the demonstration project to the stage of business promotion Due to the unsound Economic benefit evaluation, which restricts the large-scale promotion and construction of BESS. This paper establishes the life cycle cost and income model of BESS and uses the dynamic investment payback period, net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR) and other economic indicators to analyze the economy of offshore wind power with BESS in reducing forecast deviation penalty. At the same time, aiming at stimulating the enthusiasm of the wind farm to allocate energy storage, we studied the improvement of the penalty rules of wind power forecast deviation. The research results can provide an engineering economic reference for the investment decision of BESS.

articleTitle: Main Loop Design of Zhuhai Three-terminal DC Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The flexible DC power distribution system can improve utilization of the power distribution system, support efficient and flexible access of multiple sources and loads, realize flexible and controllable power flow of each zone, and balance load rate, which is an important development direction of international power distribution research. In this paper, the main loop design of the flexible DC power distribution system is carried out, and the parameters of different power supplies and loads are designed. The dynamic characteristics of the system during the startup process and the short circuit fault are analyzed by simulation, and the rationality of the parameter design is verified. The research results have great significance in the general reference for the engineering practice and theoretical research of the flexible DC power distribution system.

articleTitle: A Self-Adapted Compositive Modulation Method for Full-Bridge Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper proposes a self-adapted compositive modulation (SACM) method for full-bridge modular multilevel converter (FB MMC) under boosted modulation index, aiming at reducing the total harmonic distortion (THD) of AC voltage with low switching frequency. The SACM synthesizes the nearest-level modulation (NLM) and self-adapted pulse width modulation (SAPWM). The integer numbers of full-bridge submodules (FBSM) are switched in with NLM while the decimal numbers of FBSMs are switched in using SAPWM. The SAPWM is designed sufficiently considering the output characters of FBSMs under boosted modulation index. It can adjust the carrier phase difference of FBSMs in upper and lower arms according to their output states. As a result., the levels of the inner electromotive force is increased in the entire fundamental period. Moreover, the modified capacitors voltage balance scheme is utilized in the SACM to maintain low switching frequency. The feasibility of the SACM is verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Control Measures for Steady-State Power Frequency Overvoltage of Half-Wavelength Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The half-wavelength transmission line (HWTL) is a forward-looking and competitive solution for transcontinental and transnational power transmission. The problem of steady-state power frequency overvoltage of HWTL is serious. It is a matter of great concern in the safety and stability analysis of the power system connected with the HWTL. In this paper, for the problem of steady-state power frequency overvoltage of HWTL, three control measures, i.e. tripping off generating units in the sending system, fast DC modulation, and improving the power factor of the receiving-end of the HWTL, are proposed. The theoretical analysis is given, and the effectiveness of the three control measures is confirmed by an example of a large power system connected with HWTL. The research enriches the theory of HWTL and has great significance in practical guiding.

articleTitle: Impact Stress Analysis and Structural Optimization Design of Thomson Coil Actuators
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Thomson Coil (TC) actuators are widely used in the field of mechanical switches by its ultra-high speed. In this paper, a multi-physical coupling model of the TC based on finite element (FE) analysis is established, and the armature flexing and its effect on structural strength are analyzed. It is found that increasing the thickness of armature, the radius of round table and radius of chamfering could increase the natural vibration frequency of the system, thus reducing the stress value and vibration amplitude. It is also shown that the distribution and pulse width of repulsive force have little effect on the stress, while the peak value of repulsive force plays a decisive role. The simulation results show a good accuracy compared with experimental results to verify the validity of these conclusions. The numerical calculation method could be used to guide engineering design.

articleTitle: Research and development of 500kV hybrid HVDC circuit breaker with current commutation drive circuit
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In high voltage level, the dc transmission technology can provide a brand-new solution for the future transformation of electricity energy, which can realize the interconnection and complementarity of large-scale renewable energy and long-distance power transmission. And in the low and middle voltage level, power quality can be improved and various types of de loads can be connected into systems efficiently and flexibly by using dc power distribution technology. With the rapid development of dc transmission and distribution technology, it is possible to construct dc power grid in the future. This paper reviews the research progress of dc circuit breaker (DCCB) in Tsinghua University in recent years. The key technology of research on DCCB with current commutation drive circuit (CCDC) is introduced from four aspects - topology, fast mechanical switch, power electronics and principle of current commutation. Finally, an engineering prototype of 500kV DCCB has been developed, and the experimental verification of ±25kA fault current interrupting within 3ms has been completed.

articleTitle: Identification Index and Method of Serious Faults and Weak Links in Power System Transient Power Angle Stability
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: At present, the research on power angle stability of power system has a deep foundation, but most of the methods are based on the analysis of the whole system. The calculation scale is large and the formulas are complex. When the power system is developed immaturely and in an unbalanced way, there are always some weak links. After some faults occur, the weak links may exceed the stability limit and cause instability. The components resulting in the system instability may often be individual, local or regional rather than global. Finding out the critical elements is of great significance for power system analysis, prevention and control. The identification of the critical lines in complex power systems usually needs a complex method, and it is difficult to consider the influence of failures. This paper puts forward the line transient power angle stability index of a complex system which can consider the impact of failures. The method is simple and can obtain the transient power angle stability index matrix of different lines of a power system after different failures only based on the power flow data and simple matrix operations. Through the index the most serious failures and the most fragile lines of the system can be obtained and sorted in order. The proposed index can be directly used to guide the transient power angle stability analysis of power system. A test case is used to testify the application effect of the index in this paper.

articleTitle: A Novel Phase-Locked Loop under Grid Fault Condition
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Tracking the frequency and phase information of the power grid quickly and accurately when the power grid has unbalanced, distorted grid voltage and fluctuant frequency is very important for power system control and protection and power electronics converter application. However, the traditional phase locked loop will lose its effect in this case. To solve this problem, a novel grid frequency detection method is proposed in this paper. Firstly, with the theory of fan-in vector transformation, the three-phase system is transferred to the single-phase system, which simplifies the detection method. Secondly, the cascaded delayed signal cancellation method is used to extract the fundamental positive sequence voltage from the harmonics. Then, the state observer with self-adaptive frequency is designed to get the frequency and phase information from the fundamental positive sequence voltage. In the end, the simulation results verify that the proposed novel method is able to track the frequency and phase information of the power grid quickly and accurately under the condition of unbalanced, distorted grid voltage and fluctuant frequency.

articleTitle: A Current Compensation Method for Single-Phase-to-Earth Fault in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The residual current compensation degree at fault point will affect the arc suppression performance after single-phase-to-earth fault occurs in the distribution networks with small current grounding system. This paper theoretically deduced the variation law of zero sequence admittance parameters before and after faults in flexible grounding system, and takes this as the basis of parameter closed-loop control to realize the full compensation of grounding current. The proposed method can accurately compensate the active and reactive components of the grounding current, and realize reliable arc suppression. The control strategy and proposed method has been validated through simulation and verified on 10 kV distribution networks.

articleTitle: Core Loss Comparison for 3-Level Grid-Connected Inverter with the LCL or the ILCL Filter Using DPWM
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The improved LCL filter (ILCL) is popularly applied in transformer-less 3-level grid-connected PV inverters to suppress the leakage current. The inverter side current ripple with ILCL filter is much higher than with LCL filter in the same condition. Whereas, discontinuous pulse width modulation method (DPWM) can eliminate the current ripple with ILCL filter in high current region for the reason that there is no neutral point voltage variation. In this paper, we firstly compare the core loss for 3-level grid-connected inverter with the LCL or the ILCL filter using DPWM.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Frequency-dependent Impedance of the Traction Network Based on Electromagnetic Parameters Measurement of the Steel Rail
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: With the rapid development of Chinese Electrified railway, the power quality of railway traction power supply system has become a key research field, since it is of great need to establish an accurate electromagnetic transient model of traction network, the calculation of frequency-dependent impedance of traction network wires is one of the important steps. To address the complicated magnetization characteristics caused by the irregular section of the steel rail, experiments were conducted to measure the electromagnetic characteristic parameters of steel rail. In addition, internal impedance of the steel rail is accurately solved through the Maxwell software. After that, the multi conductor transmission lines (MTLs) of traction network are simplified by equivalent method. Accurate vector fitting of MTLs characteristic impedance and propagation function were obtained, which lays a foundation for the establishment of electromagnetic transient model of traction network.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of GaN Magnetic Resonant Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: GaN field-effect transistors (FET) enables low conduction loss and low switching loss in high-frequency (>MHz) resonant wireless power transfer systems. In this work, a GaN magnetic resonant wireless power transfer (WPT) system with 75% efficiency was designed and built. Advantages of GaN magnetic resonant wireless power transfer technology are introduced and the principle of magnetic resonant wireless power transfer technology is explained. Then, LTspice is used to simulate the designed system. Moreover, a GaN based wireless power transfer testing system was built and tested, the results of which indicate that both the coil coupling coefficient k and the load of the system affect the transmission efficiency of the system. In addition, it is found that the increment of input and output power will also increase the efficiency of the system. The system is further improved according to the actual application, the system can provide power for both lamp and mobile phone.

articleTitle: Bidirectional short circuit breaker for DC microgrid based on segmented current limiting solid state circuit breaker
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Due to the fast development speed of the short-circuit fault in DC microgrid, which make traditional protection method cannot meet time requirement, a novel short-circuit current bidirectional blocking circuit topology based on segmented current limiting solid-state circuit breaker (SCLCB) is proposed. The main circuit uses two IGBTs connected in series module to realize double-conducting. A diode based full-bridge is used as blocking circuit to realize bidirectional blocking function, and a segmented resistor current limiting module is used to limit the rising rate of the fault current. The fault current is absorbed by blocking capacitor. The proposed DC blocking circuit can limit the fault current to a safe level in a very short time. The performance of the proposed blocking circuit is verified by saber simulation. The result shows that the blocking circuit can successfully limit the fault current within 6ms, and can suppress the turn-off overvoltage of main switch. The blocking circuit has good application prospects in DC microgrid protection.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Distributing Method of Electromagnetic Transient Real-time Simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: With the rapid development and application of DC grids, the simulation scale and requirements of DC real-time simulation are increasing. The decoupling method of the network is a necessary means to improve the real-time simulation efficiency of the DC grid. In this paper, an automatic distributing method is proposed for electromagnetic transient real-time simulation. This method adopts the principle of resource utilization optimization. Automatic network division is proceeded according to the number of nodes, and the number of simulation networks is minimized. To some extent, the grid parallel calculation error is reduced. This method reduces manual participation and improves the efficiency of the network partition. An optimization scheme is provided in this paper for electromagnetic transient parallel computing, which effectively improves the accuracy and efficiency of AC and DC power grid simulation. It provides an effective solution to solve the problem of large-scale DC grid simulation.

articleTitle: AC Impedance Modeling of Modular Multilevel Converters Considering Different Control Modes: Similarities and Differences
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper presents an AC impedance modeling method of modular multilevel converter (MMC) considering different control modes, and its accuracy is verified by simulation. Then the similarities and differences of the MMC impedance model under different control modes are compared. It indicates that low frequency characteristics of MMC impedance are significantly different and the high frequency characteristics are basically the same under different control modes. When studying the low frequency oscillation (or stability) of the MMC-HVDC, outer control loop cannot be ignored; and the impedance model can be simplified to current inner-loop control impedance model when studying the high frequency stability, which is much simpler but still accurate enough.

articleTitle: AC Side Fault Characteristics Analysis of LCC-MMC Hybrid HVDC
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: when the AC short-circuit fault occurs in the multi-DC feed area, it may cause the failure of multi-DC simultaneous commutation, causing the huge power shortage and affecting the stability of the power grid. Hybrid DC transmission is one of the effective solutions to solve the failure of commutation of conventional DC transmission. This paper introduces the main topology of hybrid DC transmission, expounds the principle of LCC-MMC hybrid DC transmission system, analyzes the fault characteristics of rectifier and inverter stations, and carries out simulation.

articleTitle: Emergency power control strategies applied for offshore wind farms connected by HVDC system
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: More and more long-distance, large scale offshore wind farms (OWFs) are developed, and connect to the onshore grid through the voltage source converter (VSC) based HVDC link. Particular attention should be paid to the grid connection requirements as the OWF is decoupled with the onshore grid via the VSC-HVDC link. Power fed into the onshore grid should be controlled to some extent for power dispatching requirement. A special emergency power control (EPC) with 3 control modes and its implementation strategies are introduced as an automatic response to realize temporary or permanent power reduction by cooperating with DC chopper and offshore wind farm. EPC1 is designed to realize full power reduction in a short time with assistance of DC chopper. EPC2 is required to reduce power to a pre-defined level relying upon power control by OWFs. EPC3 is to deactivate the function of EPC2. For avoidance of communication failure, a supplementary control of the offshore system frequency is also considered to trigger power reduction of OWFs. PSCAD simulation results demonstrate the validation of proposed EPC strategies.

articleTitle: Research on Test Method for Flexible HVDC Valve Base Controller Based on RTLAB
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: With the sustained development of flexible HVDC technology, the reliability of Valve Base Controller becomes very important. In view of the shortcomings of the existing VBC test system, this paper builds a test system which can access full-scale VBC based on RTLAB simulation platform. This paper presents a comprehensive VBC test method. The test system and test method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the comprehensiveness and accuracy of VBC test. The test system has been applied in the delivery test of VBC in Zhangbei HVDC grid project. It can also provide reference for the test of VBC in other flexible HVDC projects.

articleTitle: Research on construction and operation of standard system for global energy interconnection
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This article analyzes the necessity and describes principles of the global energy interconnection (GEI) standard system, meanwhile describes the conceptual modelling of GEL Simultaneously, it develops the overall architecture of the GEI standard system comprising a number of standards in 47 standard series from 13 technical fields in four directions. It finally gives recommendations for the development of GEI standard system.

articleTitle: The Modeling and Control of E-router Based on Average-value Model
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: E-routers (E-router) are the core equipment of the energy Internet (EI), so it is necessary to study various control strategies based on the E-routers. Electromagnetic transient simulation is an important tool to study the control strategies of E-routers. However, each E-router contains multiple converters, and each converter contains multiple power electronic devices. At the same time, pulse width modulation technology is used. Both the power electronic devices and the modulation technology will increase mathematical calculation of the E-router system. Therefore, an average-value model of the E-router is proposed to replace the detailed model to simplify the simulation system. A single-input multiple-output (SIMO) E-router simulation system is built on the MATLAB/Simulink and simulated. The simulation results show that the system dynamic responses of the average-value model are highly consistent with the detailed model, and the average-value model greatly speeds up the system simulation and improves the simulation efficiency.

articleTitle: Empirical test and evaluation of efficiency of string PV inverters
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In this paper, a method of efficiency test and evaluation for string PV inverter in empirical testing platform is proposed. Based on the operating mechanism and efficiency empirical testing requirements of string PV inverter, the method of efficiency test for string PV inverter is researched, the device of efficiency test for string PV inverter is developed to test string PV inverter in empirical testing platform. Moreover, based on the method of efficiency evaluation in laboratory, the evaluation method of string PV inverter based on empirical test result is proposed through empirical test data analysis and processing. The experimental results verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Temporary Blocking Strategies of Converter Valve in MMC-based DC Grid with Overhead Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Compared with the AC grid, DC grid based on Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) with overhead transmission line has problems such as faster development of fault current and wider range of fault influence. To ensure the safety of the converter valve and the continuous operation of the system, blocking the converter valve temporarily is usually necessary. Three blocking schemes can be used according to the range of blocking, i.e. global temporary blocking, phase-based temporary blocking and arm-based blocking. Based on a four-terminal DC grid model, the strategies are compared and analyzed from the perspectives of the safety of the converter valve, the impact on the system under fault ride through, and on the fluctuation of internal circulating current. The results show that global blocking is easy to implement but the system may become uncontrollable, arm-based blocking will cause less fluctuations in system under fault ride through, and it has a better fault recovery performance. The research results can provide reference to the strategy design for the projects with similar operation requirements.

articleTitle: Voltage-Sharing Components Configuration of Double-Break Fast Mechanical Switch for a 200 kV Hybrid DC Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: With the construction of 200 kV flexible DC power grid, 200 kV DC circuit breakers have been demanded. The fast mechanical switch, which is an important component in the hybrid DC circuit breaker, usually adopts multi-break structure to meet the requirements of breaking time and effective opening stroke. For a 200 kV double-break fast mechanical switch, the voltage characteristics in the breaking process were analyzed firstly. Then, the distributed capacitances' parameters were calculated by the finite element method. Finally, the voltage-sharing components' parameters were simulated by using PSCAD/EMTDC. It is suggested that the voltage-sharing capacitors' value be selected from 260 pF to 300 pF, 200 Ω for the current limiting resistor, and 200 MΩ for the voltage-sharing resistor. The research can provide a reference for the voltage-sharing design of mechanical switches in non-arc hybrid DC circuit breakers.

articleTitle: Study on the Non-random Characteristic of PETT Oscillation
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Plasma Extraction Transit Time (PETT) oscillation in large power IGBT module, which is caused by space charge effect, causes serious electromagnetic interference to space environment and driver system.
