In order to investigate whether the PETT oscillation occurs randomly or not, the small signal behaviors of a simplified IGBT model is analyzed. Theoretical analysis indicates that PETT oscillation does not occur randomly, but has a strong relationship with DC bus voltage. Experimental results show that test voltage has an obvious influence on initial oscillation time, which verified the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Comparison Analysis of the Flexible Sub-module voltage modulation and NLM for MMC-DC grid
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The voltage source converter (VSC) based HVDC technology have been built for transferring power over long distances with high voltage in past decades. Recently, the development of modular multilevel converter (MMC) technology makes HVDC could be used for higher voltage and greater power capacity, which provides a possibility to build MMC DC grid. In this paper, the flexible sub-module voltage modulation strategy of MMC in a four-terminal MMC DC grid will be investigated and two schemes to handle the occurrence of sub-modules fault will be proposed. A four-terminal DC grid model is built in the software PSCAD/EMTDC in order to verify the effective of the flexible sub-module voltage modulation strategy applied to MMC DC grid.

articleTitle: A Novel Three-Phase Phase-Locked Loop Based on DSOGI and Adaptive Observer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Tracking the frequency and phase information of the power grid quickly and accurately when the power grid has unbalanced, distorted grid voltage and fluctuant frequency is very important for power system control and protection and power electronics converter application. However, the traditional phase locked loop will lose its effect in this case. To solve this problem, a novel three-phase phase-locked loop (PLL) based on DSOGI and adaptive observer algorithm is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the double second-order generalized integrator (DSOGI) is designed to filter multiple harmonics and realize positive and negative sequence voltage separation. Then, the state observer with self-adaptive frequency is designed to get the frequency and phase information from the fundamental positive sequence voltage. In the end, the simulation results verify that the proposed novel PLL is able to track the frequency and phase information of the power grid quickly and accurately under the condition of unbalanced, distorted grid voltage and fluctuant frequency.

articleTitle: Dynamic Reactive Power Control Strategy for Back to Back VSC-HVDC Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Based on the principles of power decoupling control, VSC-HVDC system has the capability to support AC system voltage. In this paper, the operation capability and reactive control strategy of “Yu/E” back to back VSC-HVDC system are researched. A novel voltage-supporting reactive power controller is proposed. The real-time AC voltage is considered in the limitation of reactive power, and the reactive power target value will be limited when the AC voltage works beyond its restriction. The presented reactive power control strategy has valid dynamic response capability, and could improve the stability performance of connected power grids. A closed-loop simulation platform is built and steady/transient state cases are studied. The test results show the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: DC Faults Detection in Bipolar Cascaded Modular H7 Current Source Converter for HVDC application
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In view of the DC fault current clearance deficiency for the conventional HVDC topologies, such as half-bridge sub-module (HBSM) based modular multilevel converter (MMC), this paper proposes a new CSC topology for HVDC application, which can not only suppress the rise of DC fault current, but also has a better direct current (DC) line faults detection based on boundary protection principle and non-unit electrical transients. It utilizes only the DC current signal by means of the high frequency component resulted from stationary wavelet transform (SWT) to identify the DC line faults. Furthermore, the distinction method of different kind of DC faults by applying transient voltage changes is proposed. The proposed method does not depend on commutation and would action more quickly.

articleTitle: Research on Coding Method and its Application for 3d Digital Design of Power Transmission and Transformation Projects
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Coding for model of three-dimension design of power transmission and transformation projects is the key to achieve transmission and share of digital design results which act as open semantide among the full lifecycle of project. In domestic power grid industry, various coding systems are different in structure of code and range of application which results in disunity in use. This paper proposes a coding method for three-dimension design of power transmission and transformation projects on account of research on existing coding systems. Moreover, interface technology between coding method of three-dimension digital design and other coding system in power grid industry is discussed. Last but not least, a method to realize software automatic coding for model of three-dimension design is put forward.

articleTitle: Research on a dual step-up Cuk converter for different new energy generation
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Due to the discontinuity and instability of the new energy generation in the application process, a dual step-up Cuk converter with low input ripple and low output ripple and high efficiency for different new energy generation based on the reliability of the system power supply is proposed in this paper. The operating principle and the operating process is analyzed, key parameter is designed. Computer simulation has been carried out to verify for a dual step-up Cuk converter with a power of 200W. The management strategy was elaborated to verify the feasibility of the power supply system.

articleTitle: Study on Control and Protection Strategy of Neutral Bus Switch in HVDC Flexible Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Neutral bus switch plays an important role in the operation mode switching of HVDC flexible transmission system such as normal pole outage and fault isolation. The rationality of neutral bus switch protection strategy is directly related to the operation reliability of HVDC flexible transmission system. At present, there are few researches on neutral bus switch control strategy of HVDC flexible system. This paper put forward the control sequence and protection strategy of neutral bus switch based on the operation characteristics of HVDC flexible transmission project, and the control and protection circuits are designed accordingly. Finally, a test method of neutral bus switch is put forward. Based on the Xiamen HVDC flexible transmission project, relevant experiments are carried out and the results prove the feasibility of the proposed control strategy and test method.

articleTitle: Fault Identification Method for Flexible DC Grid Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Fast identification of DC faults has become a bottleneck restricting the rapid development of multi-terminal flexible DC grid. Based on the self-learning characteristics of convolutional neural network (CNN), a fault identification method based on convolutional neural network for flexible DC grid is proposed. The structure of the designed convolutional neural network consists of two input branches. The inputs of the two branches are a two-dimensional matrix composed of positive and negative line voltages and a two-dimensional matrix composed of positive and negative line currents. The sampling data window of voltage and current is set to 2 milliseconds after the start of the fault identification program. The scheme only utilizes single-ended electrical quantity, which not only realizes the rapid identification of DC fault types and areas, but also can reliably distinguish faults from lightning disturbance. Finally, a four-terminal flexible DC grid model is built in PSCAD/EMTDC to demonstrate the effectiveness of the fault identification method.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Steady-state Voltage Regulation of New-generation Synchronous Condensers on HVDC Commutation Failure
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The dynamic reactive power support capability of the grid during faults and the voltage level after faults have an important impact on DC commutation failure. A new-generation synchronous condenser can effectively improve the system dynamic reactive power support capacity and grid voltage level. However, the new-generation synchronous condenser and DC are controlled independently, and there is no reasonable coordinated control strategy between them. In this paper, the mechanism of DC commutation failure has been studied. The new-generation synchronous condenser's reactive power output characteristics have been studied. Then, the reasonable coordination strategy between the new-generation synchronous condensers with DC system is proposed. The DC commutation failure probability is reduced based on this strategy. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Research on Contact Structure in Vacuum Interrupter for DC Breaking Capability
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The fast DC vacuum circuit breaker is required that the vacuum interrupter can not only break large current within several milliseconds, but also guarantee the required mechanical life under the condition that the mechanical impact is much larger than that of the AC vacuum interrupter. This paper investigates the DC breaking capability of three typical vacuum interrupters with axial magnetic field contact structure-without slots, with radial slots and with parallel slots by simulation. And the current breaking capability of contacts without slots is proved by prototype test. A test circuit and a method for current breaking capability of fast switchgears are proposed. The research results can provide technical reference for the engineering application of fast DC vacuum switchgears.

articleTitle: Review of Fault Traverse Control Technology for Wind Power Flexible Direct Grid-connected System
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Flexible DC transmission technology can isolate the impact of faults to a certain extent. It is a grid-connected mode worthy of in-depth study for large-scale wind farms. In this paper, the operation control of flexible direct wind power delivery system is reviewed from the aspects of control strategy and fault protection. Firstly, the fault traversal performance of VSC-HVDC system is summarized. Secondly, the existing fault control strategies are analyzed and compared, the advantages and disadvantages of fault control strategies are systematically reviewed, and the operation control technology after AC fault is emphatically discussed. Finally, the research direction of flexible HVDC control technology is proposed.

articleTitle: Analysis and Impact of Shocking Characteristic in Ultra- fast Disconnecting Switch of Hybrid HVDC Breaker
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Ultra-fast disconnecting switch is one of the key components in hybrid HVDC circuit breaker. During ultra-fast disconnecting action, a considerable shock to the supporting structure will be produced by the internal moving parts of ultrafast disconnecting switch. In this paper, the movement process of the moving parts within ultra-fast disconnecting switch is described, and the shocking characteristic of ultra-fast disconnecting switch is studied using experimental method. The maximum instantaneous impact force reaches 102kN. In order to reduce the impact of ultra-fast disconnecting switch on supporting structure of HVDC circuit breaker, damping isolators are applied. Results of simulation analyses and experiments show that both stress and vibration amplitude have been improved obviously because of the application of damping isolators.

articleTitle: A modified DC fault protection scheme for multi-terminal HVDC grid based on fault current limiters
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper proposes a modified dc fault protection scheme for multi-terminal HVDC grid based on hybrid fault current limiters(HFCLs). To release the pressure of dc circuit breakers(DCCBs), HFCLs are applied to limit the fault current in advance. During the interrupting process, a coordinating method of DCCB and HFCL by utilizing the charged capacitor in HFCL is proposed so that the fault current could be interrupted more quickly, thus accelerating the protecting process. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}\pm 500\text{kV}$</tex> 4-terminal HVDC grid is built in PSCAD/EMTDC and the performance of proposed and other protection schemes are compared. The simulation results verify that the proposed modified protection scheme could effectively limit the fault current, shorten the protecting time and reduce the energy dissipation in DCCB.

articleTitle: A novel secondary frequency control strategy for islanded microgrid based on identification model
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Secondary frequency regulation control strategy plays a key role in maintaining the stability of frequency and improving power quality, especially in droop-controlled microgrid system. However, due to the confidentiality of manufacturers, the internal structure of microgrid cannot be obtained, thus the conventional second frequency regulation strategy based on mechanism modeling may be unavailable. To solve these problems, this paper presents an online identification method for droop-controlled microgrid system, which can also be used for online optimization of secondary frequency regulation controller. The whole frequency regulation process is described in detail, and simulation results are carried out to show the validity of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Parallel VSGs with Consensus Control
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In recent years, consensus control has become a research hotspot in microgrids cooperative control. When consensus control is applied to virtual synchronous generator (VSG) system, the system has more complicated dynamic performance since it has higher order. Aiming at this problem, this paper establishes a small signal state-space model, and analyzes the influence of various control parameters. Furtherly, suggestions on parameters design are given based on the model. Finally, the simulation results verifies the accuracy of model the effectiveness of the design method.

articleTitle: Fundamental and Analysis of a Novel Magnetic Coupling Fault Current Limiter for VSC DC Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: A DC fault current limiter (DC FCL) in a voltage-source converter (VSC) DC grid is defined as a device which limits fault currents during the transients from fault initiation to DC circuit breaker (DCCB) current interruption. The so far proposed and studied DC FCLs have some inherent disadvantages, including but not restricted to: non-changing impedance, high on-line operating conduction loss, complex structure and unreliability, which constrain system performance. In this paper, a novel magnetic coupling FCL (MCFCL) is proposed with the firstly employed current-limiting principle in VSC DC grids. It has the pure metallic primary winding connected in series to a transmission line, magnetically coupled with the power electronic controlled variable passive load in the secondary side, achieving low conduction loss and fast-changing impedance respectively. Although the introduction of the power electronic circuitry in MCFCL increases the complexity and failure rate compared with the reactor type FCL, the magnetic coupling, by natural, can to some extent decrease the effect from the secondary side failure on the primary. The fundamentals and modelling of the MCFCL are demonstrated, followed by some analytical and numerical analyses showing its advantages over conventional reactor type FCLs.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of SOFC Based Stationary Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: With the increasing interest in solid oxide fuel cells, it would be beneficial and important to study its modeling as well as the control of the fuel cell based distributed generation in power grid. In this paper, a solid oxide fuel cell model is firstly presently. It was shown how a block-oriented solid oxide fuel cell is modeled in MATLAB/Simulink. By combining the auxiliary components, a solid oxide fuel cell based power plant was developed. Furthermore, a control methodology using the concept of virtual synchronous generator is proposed to integrate the fuel cell based power plant to the electric power grid. The theoretical considerations are complemented by application to illustrate the value of the modelling and control.

articleTitle: Energy Supply System of HVDC Equipment Based on Symmetric Capacitors Coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of power supply for control drivers of HVDC transmission equipment, a novel energy supply system for HVDC equipment is proposed based on capacitor DC isolation characteristic and inductance-capacitance series resonance principle, which realizes efficient transmission from ground-potential side power supply to high-potential side power supply. In this paper, the working principle of the proposed energy supply system is analyzed, and a parameter design for the topology is carried out. The simulation results of the specific examples are verified by the PSIM simulation software, which verifies the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed energy supply system.

articleTitle: Electro-magnetic Transient Modeling Method for Nonlinear Components applied in DC power grid
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: With the rapid development of dc power grid, nonlinear components represented by metal oxide arrester (MOA) are becoming an important part of the grid. However, MOA electro-magnetic transient (EMT) model has complicated nonlinear characteristics and is difficult to be integrated with other components to establish the integrated EMT model, which remarkably influences the ease of application of nonlinear models. An EMT modeling method for nonlinear components is proposed in this paper. It gives out the method to simplify complex circuit that contains nonlinear components. The method is validated by PSCAD/EMTDC simulation.

articleTitle: Frequency Couplings in Impedance Modeling of Voltage Source Converters
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: A grid-connected voltage source converter (VSC) system may be unstable when the grid is weak. Sequence impedance has proven to be an effective tool for analyzing such problems. As a small signal analysis method, sequence impedance can be obtained by calculating the current response to a voltage perturbation at the same frequency. However due to the phase locked loop (PLL) and dc link voltage controller, the current response at a different frequency from voltage perturbation may be noticeable, which means there exist frequency couplings in the impedance modeling. This paper proposes an impedance model of VSC considering frequency couplings caused by these two factors and analyzes how these factors affect the impedance. The proposed model and analysis results are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Experimental Platform for DC Grid: Design and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: With the development of power electronics technology and the rise of energy internet, DC grid, as a new form of power system with high energy density, low loss, flexible control, and convenient access to renewable energy, has become a research focus. Based on the requirements of system research and equipment development, this paper designs and establishes an experimental platform for DC grid. The platform includes various types of AC/DC converters, DC/DC converters, renewable energy simulation devices, networking devices, control and protection devices, and a real-time digital simulation system based on RT -LAB, its physical structure is designed to be topological flexible and control system is designed to be automatically cooperative. The established result is suitable for system analyzing in fields such as LVDC microgrid, MVDC distribution, and HVDC transmission, and is able to perform hardware-in-loop testing on key equipment of DC grids. Design and establishment of this platform provides a strong support for theoretical and technological R&D in related fields, and is of great significance for the technical and industrial development of DC grid.

articleTitle: Single-Phase Transformer-less Inverter with Leakage Current Suppression and Active Power Decoupling Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In this paper, a single-phase transformer-less inverter for PV application based on full bridge inverter is proposed, which is capable of solving both second-order power ripple and leakage current issues. In this topology, the inherent power ripple in the single-phase inverter is eliminated using an additional power decoupling circuit. The voltage across the power decoupling capacitor is controlled as a pure sinusoidal waveform to cancel out the second-order ripple power and attain full utilization of the capacitor. Therefore, the bulky electrolytic capacitors with relatively short lifetime can be replaced by film capacitors. In addition, the leakage current is reduced significantly because of the use of a small auxiliary capacitor for the voltage-clamp and current-bypass functions, which ensure that most of leakage current flows through the auxiliary capacitor instead of parasitic capacitor. The simulation results verify the validity of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Waveform Similarity Analysis for Nonlinear Components of Metal Oxide Arrester (MOA)
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Recently, nonlinear components such as metal oxide arresters (MOA) are widely used in MMC-HVDC systems. Equivalent models are proposed to accelerate the simulation of complex nonlinear components. However, it is hard to evaluate the similarity of the original model and equivalent model. In this paper, a novel method is proposed to calculate the similarity of similar waveforms after removing the time delay and DC offset, and is capable to give the degree of the accuracy of the equivalent model. We eliminate the influence of DC offset by differentiating and calculate the time delay by finding the most similar interval between two discrete series. And then the DC offset of similar waveforms is obtained by integrating in the fitting interval. Finally, based on the concept of the coefficient of determination in statistics, the two waveforms similarity are evaluated. Then waveforms obtained from the detailed model and the equivalent model of nonlinear component in MOA are analyzed with the method.

articleTitle: A Cascaded Back-to-Back H-bridge Converter With Full Four-quadrant Operation Capability
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper presents a medium voltage converter which consists of cascaded power units, each of which has two H bridges sharing a same DC link. This back-to-back H-bridge topology not only guarantees the four-quadrant operation capability but also simplifies the cable layout of the converter. Both rectifying and inverting sides of the converter adopt the unipolar carrier phase shifted SPWM method in order to achieve high equivalent switching frequency and superimpose high voltage. A hybrid controller structure containing two controlling periods has been built in order to reduce the calculation burden. Besides a phase correction strategy is proposed to compensate the control delay difference. The proposed converter is verified by simulation and a practical engineering project. The key performances, such as input current harmonic, DC voltage balance and output voltage harmonic” are satisfactory.

articleTitle: Analysis of Differential Mode Interference Characteristics in Energy Supply Circuit of Hybrid DC Breaker caused by Electromagnetic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: High di/dt will be generated during open operation of high-voltage hybrid DC breaker under the fault short-circuit current. Differential mode interference (DMI) in auxiliary energy supply circuit due to electromagnetic coupling may invade into the semiconductor control device. In order to avoid the false action of DC Breaker, research and evaluation of DMI should be paid more attention during design stage. This paper presented the analysis of coupling mechanism between multi-valves and energy supply circuit, and the calculation and comparison of coupling DMI strength under different cable layout. Further, a recommended energy supply circuit configuration is descripted. Response simulations of different circuit configurations under the DMI excitation are performed. Applying the configuration in 500kV High Voltage DC Breaker, the test results shows that the impact of DMI could be reduced by Inductive impedance of circuit configuration very well.

articleTitle: Analysis of DC Pole-to-Pole Fault for converters in MVDC Shipboard Power System
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In Medium voltage direct current (MVDC) shipboard power system, extensive use of power electronics is required for connecting devices to the MVDC bus. Due to the high discharge ability of the dc-link capacitor of converters, the pole-to-pole short circuit (PPSC) fault will make a fatal effect on the system. Moreover, the lack of operational experience and appropriate fault analysis techniques of different converters also limit the development of MVDC protection. This paper explores the dynamic behavior for different types of converter during PPSC fault. The fault current transient processes are analyzed in detail with the detailed operation simulations. An expediently fault current analysis method based on equivalent circuit model is proposed. The results of simulations show that the proposed method is effective for different types of converters, and it can replace the detailed simulation model in the future study of MVDC protection technology.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Frequency Influence of LVRT Strategy on Power Grid with High-permeability PV
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The low voltage ride through (LVRT) ability of PV inverter is very important to the safety and stability operation of grid. The current LVRT control strategy emphasizes reactive current support during voltage dip, and there is no active power requirement, so in the grid with high PV permeability, it is easy to cause large active power shortage during the voltage dip, then the frequency will decrease. In order to solve this problem, this paper analyzes the output characteristics of PV inverter using LVRT control strategy dominated by national standard, and the influence to frequency stability of grid with high PV penetration. Based on IEEE standard 3-machine 9- bus network frame, the grid frequency performance is simulated with the model of PV power station, The frequency variation during voltage dip using two typical LVRT control strategies were compared. At last, it is suggested to strengthen the active power support of PV power station during the grid dip, the output of reactive power and active power is guaranteed at the same time, the active and reactive power support to grid is realized, the LVRT performance of PV power station is improved to support grid.

articleTitle: Research on Harmonic Monitoring Technology of Xiamen MMC-HVDC Transmission Project
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In order to realize the comprehensive monitoring of DC side harmonics of Xiamen MMC-HVDC transmission project, this paper proposes a convenient and feasible harmonic monitoring scheme based on actual engineering conditions. According to this scheme, a DC side harmonic monitoring system is constructed. The system can not only perform harmonic analysis and over-limit alarm on the DC side harmonics of the whole station, but also has the function of fault recording, the degree of integration is high. Through this system, the distribution of the harmonics of the DC side of the whole station can be clearly understood. It provides guarantee for the safe and stable operation of the MMC-HVDC transmission project. The FFT and artificial neural network algorithm are used to analyze the harmonic signals within 50 times. The calculation is small and the real-time performance is high, which can meet the needs of actual engineering.

articleTitle: Effect of Parasitic Inductance Mismatch on Short-Circuit Characterization of Paralleled SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In order to clarify the effect mechanism of circuit parameters on short-circuit (SC) characterization of paralleled Silicon Carbide (SiC) MOSFETs, this paper analyzes the influence of multiple parasitic inductance mismatches in detail. Both simulation and experimental results show that the influence of parasitic inductance mismatch on the SC performance of paralleled SiC MOSFETs and validate the circuit analysis. Finally, several suggestions are given for the internal layout of the multichip power module.

articleTitle: Reliability Modeling and Redundant Design of MMC-HVDC Converters Considering Direct-Coupled Sub-Module Correlations
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Recently, the half-bridge (HB) and full-bridge (FB) sub-modules (SMs) based hybrid modular multilevel converter (MMC) become a preferred topology for high voltage direct current (HVDC) system. In order to incorporate SM correlations into the optimal redundant configuration of both HBSMs and FBSMs, this paper proposes a reliability modeling approach of hybrid MMC considering direct-coupled SM correlations. Firstly, the detailed structure and reliability model of each SM are provided with component failure rates as input. Secondly, the Copula theory is introduced so that the correlations among the requisite and redundant SMs are considered. Thirdly, the sensitivity analysis of the hybrid MMC reliability with varying correlation coefficients, service years or time and numbers of redundant SMs are respectively discussed. Finally, the optimal redundant configuration of HBSM and FBSM segments considering the IGBT utilization rate and overall converter reliability is obtained. It is calculated by solving curvatures of the three-dimensional (3-D) reliability surfaces. Calculations have validated the feasibility of all the proposed approaches.

articleTitle: A Review of Control Strategies for Inertia Support in VSC-HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The last few decades have seen the growing penetration of renewable energy sources (RES) to the power system, which mainly connect to the main grid via VSC-HVDC transmission link. With an increasing number of conventional synchronous generators (SGs) replaced by RES, power system inertia has reduced significantly, and the system response to frequency disturbance is worsened. This paper presents a review of control strategies for VSC-HVDC system to improve inertial response, most of which enable a VSC station to emulate the dynamics of an SG. Based on the potential of VSC-HVDC to participate in inertia support, RES is further considered to provide inertial response with the coordination of VSC-HVDC. The characteristics of some particular strategies are discussed and concluded, offering some suggestions for future work.

articleTitle: MMC-HVDC Testing and Simulation Based on Physical Simulation System
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: For the ever increasing power rating and voltage level of modular multilevel converter (MMC) based HVDC, it becomes more and more difficult for digital simulation system to reflect the energy fluctuation and control characteristic, as well as the valve based controller (VBC) full function testing. This paper developed a 200-level, 1200 sub-modules (SM) physical simulation system based on similarity theory for MMC-HVDC control and protection device test and project simulation. Taking the ±320kV/1000MW MMC-HVDC project in Xiamen, China as the study case, the control and protection device full-function test and project simulations are performed. An improved SM capacitor voltage balancing control is proposed for large-scale MMC-HVDC project. The physical simulation experiments and digital simulation results verify the correction of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Simulating the Efficiency of Thermoelectrical Generators for Sensor Nodes
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In order to be more environmentally friendly, a lot of parts and aspects of life become electrified to reduce the usage of fossil fuels. This can be seen in the increased number of electrical vehicles in everyday life. This of course only makes a positive impact on the environment, if the electricity is produced environmentally friendly and comes from renewable sources. But when the green electrical power is produced, it still needs to be transported to where it's needed, which is not necessarily near the production site. In China, one of the ways to do this transport is to use High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) technology. This of course means, that the current has to be converted to DC before being transported to the end user. That implies that the converter stations are of great importance for the grid security. Therefore, a precise monitoring of the stations is necessary. Ideally, this could be accomplished with wireless sensor nodes with an autarkic energy supply. A role in this energy supply could be played by a thermoelectrical generator (TEG). But to assess the power generated in the specific environment, a simulation would be highly desirable, to evaluate the power gained from the temperature difference in the converter station. This paper proposes a method to simulate the generated power by combining a model for the generator with a Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model converter.

articleTitle: A Review of Design Methods for Energy Absorption Path Design in High Voltage Direct Current Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: High Voltage Direct Current Circuit Breaker (HVDC CB) is the core element in the construction of DC power grid. Energy Absorption Path (EAP) has become an indispensable part of HVDC CB because of its function of absorbing residual energy and suppressing overvoltage. In this paper, based on the different types of HVDC CB in which EAP is located, the existing researches at home and abroad are summarized and sorted out, and then the characteristics of EAP energy absorption are explored. The energy absorption process of EAP in three different types of HVDC CB is simulated and compared. At the same time, the auxiliary functions of energy-absorbing elements in EAP, such as voltage limiting, current limiting and timing control functions, are described and verified respectively. Finally, taking DC power grid as the application scenario, this paper introduces the EAP design of two different types of HVDC CB, and points out that they have good research and development prospects.

Author Keywords: high voltage direct current circuit breaker

articleTitle: Current Suppression Method for DC Side Short Circuit Fault of MMC
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: A DC fault current limitation method based on partial bypass of sub-modules is proposed in this paper. For VSC-HVDC, the development mechanism of fault is analyzed. Considering the influence of component parameters and DC outlet voltage on fault current rising rate, the voltage modulation strategy of converter bridge arm during fault period is designed to suppress the fault current. Finally, a two-terminal flexible HVDC transmission system is built on MATLAB/Simulink to simulate and analyze the circuit fault, and the fault current is reduced from 13.15 kA to 10.12 kA at 6 ms by the proposed method after the fault.

articleTitle: A Novel Short-Circuit Protect Method for SiC MOSFET Module Based on Simplified Rogowski Coil Current Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: SiC MOSFET devices have better performance compared to conventional Si devices. But due to the difference of short-circuit characteristics, it is necessary to use special short-circuit protection method for SiC MOSFET. A novel short-circuit protection method is proposed based on the simplified Rogowski Coil current sensor in this paper. Compared with other short-circuit protection method, it has lower circuit complexity, less sensitivity to temperature, insulating with the power stage, without introducing parasitic parameters, and faster dynamic response and It also can be used as overload protection. Firstly, the operating principle of the proposed protection method is introduced. Secondly, the structure of the PCB Rogowski Coil and its signal processing circuit are analyzed. Finally, simulation and experiment for the designed PCB Rogowski Coil are verified, and the short-circuit protection function for SiC MOSFET is carried out under different short-circuit conditions.

articleTitle: Empirical Study of Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Usage in Ireland
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper presents a study of charging station usage in Ireland between 2016 and 2018. Using data collected by crawling the webpage of the Irish Board of Electricity, it can be shown that clear trends exist with regards to charging station usage. We show that peak-hours have a 20% higher usage probability than off-peak hours with the overall usage likelihood being quite low. Similarly, station usage on Sunday as off-peak day is several percent lower than on other days of the week. Looking at area-properties, we show a positive correlation between station usage and population density, electric vehicle density, and traffic density. For charging power an inverse relationship can be shown as slower chargers require longer parking-times. This offers potential for innovative station usage during off-peak hours and at sites without strong frequentation.

Author Keywords: static and dynamic linear panel models

articleTitle: Operating Area of Modular Multilevel Converter Station Considering the Constraint of Internal Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: The study of operating area of modular multilevel converter (MMC) plays an important role in the parameter design of modular multilevel converter based high voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) system. This paper studies the influence of AC system parameters and internal dynamics of MMC on the operating area of MMC. Firstly, a steady-state model connecting with AC system is developed based on a single-terminal system, and a new method to calculate the maximum value of electrical quantities with non-sinusoidal waveforms is proposed. Then, based on the point-scanning method, the operating area of MMC is obtained when the constraints of internal dynamic and external variables are considered. The influences of circulating current suppression control (CCSC) strategy and short-circuit ratio (SCR) of AC system are studied respectively, and the main constraints to confine the operating area are determined. Finally, the boundary control is designed for power over-limit situation. Simulation results in PSCAD/EMTDC verify the validity and accuracy of the proposed calculation method and the boundary control.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Control Design for Multi-Terminal Voltage-Sourced Converter High Voltage Direct Current Systems with Zero Dynamics Regulation
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper presents a nonlinear control strategy with a nested control structure for a class of multi-terminal VSC HVDC systems. An output control law is first proposed, which is based on the passive output. When the output variables converge to zero with the developed output control law, the system behavior is governed by the uncontrolled zero dynamics. However, due to some desired control variables such as the DC voltage that belong to the internal dynamics, an outer control loop is then suggested to arbitrarily drive the zero dynamics, which provides a reference to be tracked by the output control law. The performance of the proposed control algorithm is evaluated by numerical simulations which show that the system has a much faster convergence rate than the controller without the outer loop.

articleTitle: Research on Melting Scheme for Overhead Line of Flexible DC Grid Without Power Failure
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Ice coating caused by ice and snow disasters is extremely harmful to DC power grids. Therefore, the research and application of ice melting technology is of great significance for DC grids to combat ice disasters. According to the advantages and limitations of a variety of DC transmission line melting methods, the paper decided to select the two types of operation modes, namely, power flow control and converter station bipolar parallel connection, to analyze the ice melting of overhead lines. Firstly, the paper calculates the minimum ice-melting current of the overhead line and the corresponding ice-melting time of different ice-melting currents. Then the ice-melting analysis is performed on two typical overhead lines using the power flow control method, and one of the overhead lines is melted. For another line, the ice-melting is implemented using the bipolar parallel operation method. On this basis, the paper proposes a switching operation scheme for switching to bipolar parallel operation. Finally, it is concluded that the power flow control method and the bipolar parallel operation of the converter station can improve the current of the transmission line, thus achieving the melting of the overhead line of the four-terminal flexible DC grid.

articleTitle: InFIS - Integrated Research Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In this paper we present the current state of the project InFIS - Integrated Research Infrastructure. Specifically we show how a PV Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) can be connected to a grid emulator and a central simulation environment. The grid emulator is a modular multilevel converter consisting of six arms containing four Insulated-gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) submodules each. The grid simulation operates on commercial PHiL hardware simulating the CIGRE distribution grid benchmark network. Communication is established in real-time using the Villas Framework. Results presented show how each component is built and connected to the central simulation system as well as some initial results on system scaling and dimensioning.

Author Keywords: Distributed Power Hardware in the Loop (PhiL)

articleTitle: Control Strategy for VSG Modified Response Based on Reliability Prediction and Adaptive Virtual Inertia
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In this paper, a control strategy for modified response of virtual synchronous generator (VSG) based on reliability prediction and adaptive virtual inertia is proposed, simultaneously pursing high-efficient tracking power generation of distributed generators and improved resilience of resisting power fluctuation disasters. By monitoring reliability of system, automatic inertia control (AIC) is carried out. Namely, when reliability of the predicted system is reduced to a critical value, it is switched to behave large inertia and presents a defensive posture to meet the requirements of failure resistance. When frequency of system is restoring, it is shown as small inertia for fast frequency restoration, which is a trade-off between small inertia required for flexible response to power of renewable energy and large inertia required for fault resistance. Besides, considering the development of distribution generation and the typical slower speed of frequency recovery compared to frequency fall, a multilevel consensus algorithm is proposed to help dispatch inertia for system with higher robustness and differential management of inertia gain calculation is carried out for inertia effective adjustment. Finally, three typical systems applying VSG technique are built with MATLAB/Simulink for verification. Simulation results demonstrate the rationality and effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Research on Mechanism and Suppression Strategy of Submodule Capacitors' Continuous Overvoltage in the MMC-HVDC Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Based on the operation principle of modular multi-level converter (MMC), the mechanism of submodule capacitors' continuous overvoltage under the single-phase grounding fault at the valve side of converter transformer or bridge arm reactor in the neutral-line grounded MMC-HVDC system is discussed. Continuous overvoltage and bypass overvoltage have contradictory demands for the setting value of overvoltage bypass protection of converter valves. In order to provide reference for the setting value, several influencing factors are analyzed to filtrate the severest circumstance of continuous overvoltage, including converter states, converter transformer ratio, voltage of PCC point, reactive power of the fault converter, power flow in DC grid and DCBs' state. Furthermore, the valve controlled unbalance protection with the minimum number of current measuring devices to identify faults quickly is proposed to suppress the continuous overvoltage, which is helpful to reduce the equipment area and avoid the effect of measuring devices' inconsistency on the accuracy of protection. Finally, a four-terminal MMC-HVDC grid is set up in PSCAD/ EMTDC. Simulation results show that the valve controlled unbalance protection can effectively suppress the continuous overvoltage and has good fault ride-through ability under AC/DC side faults and reliable protection selectivity under internal faults of converter stations.

Author Keywords: single-phase grounding fault at the valve side of converter transformer

articleTitle: Analysis of influence of large-scale wind farm grid connection on system short-circuit current
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In this paper, short-circuit current calculation and analysis are carried out on the whole network model based on PSASP software, most existing literature studies are carried out under the condition of a single equivalent modeling for wind farm, while this paper conducts simulation analysis on the actual wind farm, the model of the whole network is 220kV and above voltage grade network and 110kV and below voltage network with transmission function reserved, including the detailed parameters of transformers and lines of each voltage grade of wind farm. From the distance from the wind farm to the short circuit point, the installed capacity of the wind farm, and short circuit point voltage grade, the contribution value of large-scale wind farm access to short-circuit current, the influence rule of wind power grid connection on the short-circuit current of the bus in the near area is revealed in many aspects. It provides guidance and reference for power system planning and dispatching department.

articleTitle: Method for Power Flow Controller Location-Allocation and Optimized Flow Control method of Meshed DC Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: Voltage source converter based multi-terminal HVDC grid becomes a trend in the future. DC power flow controller can solve the overloaded HVDC lines and thereby enhancing the DC grid security by improving the degree of control freedom. But the introduction of controller can result in increasing of order number and changing of element in node admittance matrix and Jacobin matrix. This leads to the impacts on calculating speed and efficiency of conventional power flow calculation. This paper investigates a method of equivalent power injection, which the new nodes transferred to both ending of the line in the form of additional injection power, preventing the large amount calculations. The paper investigates a method to select optimal location for DCPFC based on sensitivity. In order to make the power flow control do not increase the DC grid loss, this paper uses the primal-dual interior point method to calculate the DC power grid optimization power flow with the power flow controller, and obtain the optimal adjustment value of the power flow controller.

Author Keywords: interior point method optimal power flow

articleTitle: Design of DC Reactors for DC Fault Ride-through on MMC-based Bipolar DC Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper provides the design criteria of the DC reactors for the most promising configuration option that is bipolar DC grid. The DC reactors on bipolar grid are divided into pole reactor and neural line reactor. The configurations of DC reactor are compared and shows the distributed configuration is suitable for neutral line reactor and pole reactor. Furthermore, the difference of these two reactors is investigated, showing that pole reactor is superior in limiting the fault injected by the non-fault stations and hold the dc voltage during the fault. Neutral line reactor would not affect the dynamic characteristics of the system and can protect the system from valve-side or dc bus fault that pole reactor can not. The design constraints of choosing DC reactor about hybrid DC circuit breaker (DCCB), protection requirement, additional fault current limiter (FCL) and stability are discussed. Finally, a three terminal meshed DC grid as a case study to verify the design method. For completeness, all fault analysis results are based on PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: D-Q Frame Impedance Modeling of Modular Multilevel Converter Based on Dynamic Phasors
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: A d-q frame impedance model of modular multilevel converter (MMC) is presented in this paper. The basis of the modeling method is dynamic phasors and transfer matrix. The 10th-order dynamic phasor model for the MMC is linerized. Then, a 14th-order transfer matrix in the rotating d-q frame can be derived, by combining the 10th-order linearized electrical model and the controller model. The proposed analytical impedance model obtained from the transfer matrix is implemented in MATLAB. The validity and accuracy of the model are verified against a 81-level MMC aggregate model in MATLAB/SIMULINK in frequency domain. The results show that the impedance model has good accuracy at 1-3000 Hz, thus this model can be used in the stability and resonance analysis of MMC in a wide frequency range. The influence of phase-locked loop (PLL) and arm equivalent capacitance on the MMC dynamic is also studied using the proposed impedance model. The results show that high PLL bandwidth and small arm equivalent capacitance can lead to instability. Furthermore, the simulation results verify the suitability of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability and Transient Fault Current Limitation of Voltage-Controlled MMCs with L-Filters
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper presents a design-oriented analysis on the voltage stability and the transient fault current limitation of voltage-controlled modular multilevel converter (MMC) with L-filters. First, a dual-loop voltage control based on the L-filter plant is systematically designed, where the upper limits of controller parameters for ensuring the small-signal stability are identified. Then, considering the transient fault current limitation during faults, the lower boundaries of the inner current controller parameters are derived. Within the region of allowed controller parameters, the optimization is further made to minimize the closed-loop output impedance of MMC, which enhances the robustness of MMC output voltage against the load current disturbance. Lastly, the time-domain simulations corroborate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Performances of Different Grounding Methods on MMC-based Bipolar DC Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper provides a comparison of the possible grounding methods for the most promising configuration option that is bipolar DC grid. The equivalent models and the doctrinal basis of overvoltage of healthy pole about bipolar HVDC system under dc-side pole-to-ground fault are established. According to the characteristics of rising rate and peak value of fault current and overvoltage level, the superiority-inferiority of various grounding design methods has been summarized. Furthermore, a model of the DC ring grid with three terminals is developed in PSCAD/EMTDC. As a conclusion, using inductor as fault current limiter in neutral bus and choosing small resistance resistor as grounding choice is more advantageous for fault suppression characteristics. The outcomes of the paper will be valuable for the design of grounding electrode for future DC grid based on bipolar configuration.

articleTitle: Active Reconfigurable Operation with Long Short-Term Memory Prediction for Smart City Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimal operation methodology for active reconfiguration in a DC-AC hybrid energy system in the smart city context. In a clear-sharp contrast to the conventional operation of traditional microgrids, the proposed active reconfiguration capability is able to control the power supply and provide various controllable ancillary services such as reactive power compensation, harmonic suppression, and so forth, making this new concept suitable for smart-city microgrids. The system operation of active reconfiguration is treated as a unit commitment problem through optimizing the total operational cost of the system. State recognition and prediction are performed by Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Network for the smart operation. The effectiveness of the active reconfiguration operation is validated experimentally over an electrical system model. Furthermore, the methodology of the active reconfigurable operation in microgrids presents an energy construction scheme for the future “green smart cities”.

articleTitle: Modified Nearest Level Control and Model Predictive Control on Compensation of the Number Rounding Algorithm and Sub-module Voltage for MMC-HVDC
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: This paper proposes a modified nearest level control (NLC) method and a model predictive control (MPC) method with a reduced number of considered states for modular multilevel converter (MMC) to compare their effects on the compensation of the number rounding algorithm and the voltage sorting algorithm. The NLC method is suitable for MMC-HVDC with large number of sub-modules (SM). And the proposed MPC method for the MMC-HVDC system utilizes weighting factors to configure the cost function in combination of the DC side current control and the valve side converter voltage control with a reduced number of states. Number rounding method for the sub-modules with the capacitor voltage sorting algorithm are two methods which are normally considered for the modified NLC and MPC methods to track the referenced voltage in order to guarantee the voltage balancing effect among different capacitors of SMs. However, there are always two inherent types of errors bringing with the two mentioned methods: errors resulted from the number rounding algorithm and errors generated from the deviation of the capacitor voltage of SMs from the average capacitor voltage respectively, leading to a significant difference between the output arm voltage and the input reference voltage. In this paper, two compensated methods brought from modified NLC and MPC methods respectively are proposed to compare their effects on improving the performance to significantly dampen the deviation of the output converter voltage at valve side from the referenced one, as to decrease the harmonics to avoid the oscillation and even to optimize the converter losses.

articleTitle: Studies on Artificial Neural Network Based Wind Power Grid-connected Harmonic Resonant Frequency Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: With the wide utilization of wind resources, the penetration of wind power is ever increasing. Due to the influence of various uncertainties in the wind farm, the wind farm may generate harmonic oscillations randomly in the system. Accurate detection of the resonant frequency of the system is an important prerequisite for effective harmonic suppression. In response to the aforementioned issues, this paper proposes a wind power grid-connected harmonic resonant frequency measurement based on artificial neural network. It takes the instantaneous current values measured in a certain power frequency cycle as the model input, and uses the resonant frequency of the system as the model output. The accuracy and applicability of the proposed measurement method are verified by simulation studies in the MATLAB/Simulink. Results show that the detection method proposed in this paper is highly accurate and has the potential to be used in the wind farm.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach to Power Company Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2019 4th IEEE Workshop on the Electronic Grid (eGRID)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a comprehensive evaluation strategy for power companies in different regions. Data mining technology such as decision tree, statistical analysis and data envelopment analysis are applied on different power companies. By analyzing the mining results, a comprehensive evaluation index system is established. In addition, by considering the factors of local economic and the corporation operating performance, a weight coefficient calculation method is set up based on cluster analysis. Compared to traditional power company evaluation, this method takes consideration of the endogenous and exogenous factors of different power companies, which is more objective and can also provide suggestions for future development of evaluated companies. At the end of this paper, the method is tested on power companies in China to prove it can be practically used.
